newsitem.title: UK: London gold makes little progress at afternoon fix.
newsitem.headline: London gold makes little progress at afternoon fix.

text.p: Gold prices had made little headway by the afternoon fixing on Tuesday after New York opened higher without attracting much buying, dealers said.
Interest in the platinum group metals supported the complex and palladium extended by 50 cents its high fix of late February to $157.50.
This was its highest fixing since July 10, 1995.
Gold fixed at $351.95 per ounce compared with $352.60 in the morning and Monday's $350.25.
"Everybody was bearish yesterday, now they're bullish today. It's that kind of market," one dealer said, although a day's high of $354.05 bid reflected the market's limited confidence.
A firm start to the Dow, which was approaching a record 7,100 points in early trading, and the dollar holding near the day's high of 1.71 marks discouraged movement of speculative money to gold.
Bullion sentiment began to pick up on Monday after Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he had heard of no plans for other central banks to sell gold from their reserves.
His remark came after a regular G10 meeting and referred to last week's news that Switzerland intends to sell gold to establish a humanitarian fund for Holocaust victims.
"There was some good quality producer selling yesterday but the U.S. funds stepped in. We have seen the Swiss buying today," a dealer said.

The dealer noted Swiss banks had been very active in the gold options market late last week following news of Switzerland's humanitarian fund and revaluation of its gold reserves, which would take two years to legislate.
There was buying of $325 puts and granting of calls, but the options market was quieter this week, dealers said.

"It seemed to be co-ordinated," one dealer said, adding that the business could have been done to prevent banks being on the wrong side of the market when surplus material and the gold to establish the fund was sold in a couple of years time.
Around 800 tonnes of gold would be sold over 10 years.
Silver was a little firmer without attracting much attention. It was at $5.23/$5.25, up five cents.
Platinum and palladium both opened firmer on Japanese buying.
Dealers said the continued impasse over Russian exports and the threatened strike at the Norilsk mining and refining plant was supporting the price.
Later fund buying lifted palladium to a recent fresh high.
Platinum was up $5.90 at $383.00 and palladium $5.60 ahead at $157.00/$158.00.
